messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] "fabs"
parts:
We actually "fixed" the issue. Now fabs(x) and abs(x)
are synonymous if x is real. If n is an int, then
fabs(n) returns a real, whereas abs(n) returns an int.

We discussed this ages ago and decided it'd be less
confusing to have:

real fabs(real);

int abs(int);

as the only signatures, so we deprecated this one:

real abs(real)

Do you (Andrew) think we should get rid of the deprecation
warning?

We could probably do away with fabs() altogether --- I think
it'd be sufficient for us to just have:

int abs(int);

real abs(real);

There would be no function that returned a real absolute value
for an int input, but I don't think we need that --- Stan already
lets you use an int in place of a real.

- Bob
